LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. That being said, Carolina is missing some big guns on defense, including their star pass rusher. Even if Matthew Golden cannot go or is on limited reps, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft should be able to make enough plays in the passing game. Perhaps Josh Jacobs can finally find some room to roam on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Expect a sloppy game, but the Packers will make one more play than the Panthers, getting them to 5-3 before a much-needed mini bye week. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 17, Panthers 14. away.blurb: After missing three games due to a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, quarterback Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday as they take on the Carolina Panthers in a critical intra-division game. Mayfield carried a questionable designation on the injury report into the weekend but was able to practice without limitations throughout the week. He intends to wear a specialized glove on his right hand that offers added support to the injured joint, preventing the thumb from being bent backward. Mayfield will not have the team's top receiving target at his disposal, however, as wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out for Week Seven with both a concussion and a foot injury. In addition, starting right tackle Luke Goedeke is out due to a calf ailment and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will miss his third straight outing thanks to a rib fracture. The Buccaneers and Panthers submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Seven meeting at Bank of America Stadium. After elevating linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad, the Buccaneers had 54 available players and thus had to name six inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Panthers also elevated outside linebacker Nick Hampton and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad and had to name seven inactive players. Carolina will be without one of its top pass-rushers as Jaelan Phillips is out due to a hamstring strain. Fellow outside linebacker Thomas Incoom is also unavailable due to a calf issue, and he was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. away.blurb: So can the Panthers sustain their recent success? Will Mayfield’s return yield a new hope? Will the NFC South standings be shaken up? Fans can also check the game out on radio: WRFX The Fox, 99.7 FM. Anish Shroff (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (analyst), Jake Delhomme (analyst), Jim Szoke (host), Kristen Balboni (sideline). For full local listings, check out the Carolina Panthers Radio Network . Special note: Kuechly will receive his Pro Football Hall of Fame ring at halftime of the game in Bank of America Stadium. Out: OLB Thomas Incoom (calf), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) Questionable: OT Monroe Freeling (knee), LB Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring) Out: WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), OT Luke Goedeke (calf), S Antoine Winfield (rib) Questionable: QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) Alex Zietlow: Panthers 35, Bucs 31. I know that Baker Mayfield’s almost-certain return will make this Bucs offense more dynamic. And I know that scoring 35 on this Bucs team will be difficult, considering their opportunistic defensive backfield and their Top 5 rush defense. Still, barring an implosion of turnovers, I think the Panthers outscore and outlast a Bucs team trying to get back on track. Can the Carolina Panthers make it three wins in a row? And can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers get back on track? The Panthers (3-2) are returning to Bank of America Stadium for their Week 7 contest (1 p.m., FOX) fresh off two statement victories against the Detroit Lions and the Philadelphia Eagles . They’re looking to go 4-2 for the first time as a franchise since 2019 and start 2-0 in the NFC South for the first time since 2022. Carolina ranks first in the NFL in passing yards per game (295.6), second in total yards per game (404.4) and fourth in points per game (29.2). And its defense — minus the Week 1 fiasco against the Bears that’s looking more and more like an aberration — is Top 10 in several statistics, including rushing yards allowed. The Panthers have allowed fewer than 50 yards in each of the last two weeks: 46 against the Lions, 35 against the Eagles. It’s true that the defense is a bit affected by injury, specifically at the outside linebacker spot with no Jaelan Phillips or Thomas Incoom this week . It’s also true that the defense has only had to play against starting quarterbacks three times so far this season, and two of those three — against Caleb Williams of the Bears and Deshaun Watson of the Browns — have yielded losses. That won’t happen this week; it looks like the Bucs will be led by Baker Mayfield, who’s missed the last few weeks with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand. Speaking of the Bucs (1-5): While many of their offensive stats might be skewed by Mayfield’s absence, many of their strengths will remain. Namely? Their rush defense. Tampa Bay ranks second in the NFL in rush yards allowed per game at 75.5, thanks to a defensive line anchored by nose tackle Vita Vea and an entire unit led by rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter. home.headline: Packers get exciting injury update on Micah Parsons: Report
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers expect superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons to return to practice next week, according to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport on Thursday. “Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week. Obviously short week, was not able to do it this week. Next week he should be on the practice field if all goes well. And that is an excellent thing for the Green Bay Packers,” Rapoport said. “I expect caution as far as when he’s actually on the playing field. They want to make sure everything around his knee is as strong as possible. “They are taking their time, but his return is coming.” The Packers will take the field for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Carolina Panthers later this evening. Parsons’ next opportunity to return to the field for in-game action is a Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots next Sunday. The Packers have been without their generational pass rusher for the entirety of the season thus far, as he continues to recover from the ACL tear he suffered in Week 15 of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign. Green Bay faces off against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10 before taking their bye in Week 11. Thursday night’s matchup against the Panthers will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET. The news isn’t as good for Rhyan, who is believed to have suffered a high-ankle sprain that could keep him out a month or more, Rapoport reported . The Green Bay Packers have dropped their first injury report of the week ahead of the Week 8 game against the Carolina Panthers and wide receiver Matthew Golden is on it. The injury report was an estimation , but it has Golden listed as a non-participant. This marks the second straight week Golden has been on the injury report. However, this time around, Golden has a new issue, with a foot being added to the shoulder injury he was on the injury report with last week. Along with Golden, defensive tackle Anthony Campbell, linebacker Zaire Franklin, offensive lineman Travis Glover, center Sean Rhyan and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt were all estimated non-participants. The good news is, he is not expected to be placed on injured reserve and may only miss “minimal games,” Rapoport said.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. Both of these AFC teams are contenders to win the Super Bowl this season, and the Ravens are expected to get Lamar Jackson back in action after he missed three games with a sprained ankle. The Ravens won just one of the three games that Jackson missed, and their offense has struggled over the last two weeks in losses against AFC North opponents in Cleveland and Cincinnati. The Ravens don't want to fall back to .500 this season, and they're set as small underdogs on the road against Buffalo. With every team in the AFC North sitting at over .500 this season, the Ravens can't afford too many more losses, especially against teams that they may be competing for a wild card spot against. Right now, the Bills are in first place in the AFC East, and they're coming off their bye week after a 5-1 start to the season. Josh Allen is the leading candidate to win the MVP award, and he's been terrific as both a passer and a runner. Now, he takes on a Baltimore defense that features Kyle Hamilton, Marlon Humphrey, Nate Wiggins and others in the secondary that could make it tough on a Buffalo passing game that has been short-handed at receiver for a lot of the season. The Bills are hoping to keep things rolling out of their bye, as they're two games up in the loss column on the New England Patriots in the AFC East. Oddsmakers have set Buffalo as a favorite at home, and there are several players on both of these teams that are worth a look in the prop market. So, ahead of this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made player prop picks, game picks, anytime touchdown scorer selections and more to help you wager on Bills vs. Ravens. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Ravens vs. Bills in Week 8 Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Baltimore Ravens +3.5 (-110) vs. Buffalo Bills – Iain MacMillan Josh Allen OVER 7.5 Rush Attempts (+106) – Peter Dewey Zay Flowers Anytime TD (+165) – Peter Dewey Ja’Kobi Lane OVER 2.5 Receptions (-134) – Peter Dewey Each week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column . He’s taking the Ravens to cover with Jackson expected back in the lineup: Betting on this game hinges on whether or not Lamar Jackson is going to be able to suit up for the Ravens. Unfortunately, I place my bets early in the week, so I don't have the benefit of knowing whether or not the two-time MVP will be on the field on Sunday. The betting line indicates that he will, so I'm going to trust that, along with the reports that Jesse Minter is optimistic that Jackson will be ready to go. When a team only has one loss on their schedule, and they have the best quarterback in football on their roster, a lot of their issues are overlooked. That's the case for the Bills, whose defense has been horrendous this season, ranking 30th in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. They are the only defense in football that ranks in the bottom three in both of those metrics. I hesitate to lay more than a field goal on any team with that bad of a defense, especially when that defense potentially has to face another MVP candidate at quarterback. I'll take the points with Baltimore on Sunday. Allen has been awesome on the ground this season, carrying the ball 48 times (eight times per game) for 240 yards and eight scores. Allen is the preferred option for the Bills in short yardage, handling eight or more carries in three of his six games. Fresh out of a bye, I expect Allen to be as healthy as he’s been this season, which could be a good sign for him using his legs. The Ravens are allowing over four yards per carry to opposing quarterbacks, and Allen had 14 carries in the meeting between these teams during the 2025 regular season. Baltimore ranks 12th in the league in EPA/Rush, so the Bills and Joe Brady may get creative with the running game rather than riding James Cook (who has had fumbling issues) on Sunday. At plus money, this prop is worth a shot for the former league MVP. Ravens star Zay Flowers has been one of the best receivers in the NFL this season, catching 40 of his 53 targets (in six games) for 608 yards and three scores. Flowers has three games with double-digit targets, and he’s by far the No. 1 option in this passing game. Now, with Jackson expected to return, Flowers should get a major boost against a defense that has not been able to guard anyone in the passing game. After all, the Bills are dead last in the league in EPA/Play on defense. Buffalo’s pass defense is one of the worst in the league, ranking 29th in EPA/Pass while allowing 15 passing scores. Opposing wide receivers have torched the Bills, scoring 11 touchdowns across six games – the most allowed to the position in the NFL. It doesn’t get much better for Flowers, who is averaging over 100 yards per game and has caught at least five passes in every matchup. Since these teams combined for 81 points the last time they played, I’d expect another up-and-down matchup with a ton of offensive possessions for both sides. Flowers has simply been too effective in space, and he has the fourth-highest target share in the NFL this season. That puts him in a great spot to find the end zone for the second week in a row on Sunday. Ravens rookie Ja’Kobi Lane has played just one game with Lamar Jackson, catching one of his three targets in Week 1 against the Indianapolis Colts for 11 yards. The third-round pick missed time with a wrist injury, but he’s returned to play a major role in this offense the last two weeks. Lane played 54.4 percent of the team’s snaps in Week 6 and 68.7 percent of the snaps in Week 7, receiving five targets in each game. He reeled in seven of those passes for 65 yards. While those aren’t huge numbers, Lane has cleared this prop in back-to-back games, and he saw three targets in limited snaps in the opener before going down. Jackson is an immediate boost to Baltimore’s passing offense, so I think Lane is a great bet to clear this prop for the third game in a row, especially if his snap share continues to rise. Baltimore is 4-3 this season after going 1-2 in the games Jackson missed, and it’s in last place in the AFC North with every team in the division over .500. The Ravens dropped back-to-back key division games against Cleveland and Cincinnati without the two-time league MVP. Josh Allen – the MVP favorite this season – and the Bills are coming out of their bye week to play in this game, and they’re favored at home after a 5-1 start. Buffalo is looking to get the top spot in the AFC, and it benefitted from a Kansas City Chiefs loss (now 5-1 as well) during Week 7. Sunday’s game is the eighth meeting between Jackson and Allen all-time, with the Ravens holding a 3-2 edge in the regular season while Allen has won both of his playoff matchups against Jackson. Who has the edge in this regular-season clash? All season long, the SI Betting team has been predicting the final score of NFL games, and this one is no different. He certainly gives the Ravens’ offense a higher ceiling than backup Tyler Huntley. He’s taking the Ravens to cover with Jackson expected back in the lineup: Betting on this game hinges on whether or not Lamar Jackson is going to be able to suit up for the Ravens. Unfortunately, I place my bets early in the week, so I don't have the benefit of knowing whether or not the two-time MVP will be on the field on Sunday. The betting line indicates that he will, so I'm going to trust that, along with the reports that Jesse Minter is optimistic that Jackson will be ready to go. When a team only has one loss on their schedule, and they have the best quarterback in football on their roster, a lot of their issues are overlooked. That's the case for the Bills, whose defense has been horrendous this season, ranking 30th in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. They are the only defense in football that ranks in the bottom three in both of those metrics. I hesitate to lay more than a field goal on any team with that bad of a defense, especially when that defense potentially has to face another MVP candidate at quarterback. I'll take the points with Baltimore on Sunday. The last two meetings between Allen and Jackson have been decided by two points (their playoff game in the 2024 season) and one point (their matchup in the 2025 regular season). Buffalo’s defense is last in the NFL in EPA/Play and 30th in success rate, so this could be a get-right game for Jackson and Co. if he’s able to play at his full capabilities. It’s hard to put too much stock into the Ravens last three games without him, though their defense is now 13th in yards per play allowed and 15th in success rate. That’s not terrible, especially since Joe Burrow torched this team in the second half. I expect a high-scoring affair on Sunday, and it wouldn’t shock me if this came down to a final field goal. While Henry, Cook, and Allen are all set at minus odds to find the end zone, I've decided to look at three players at plus money that could score in Week 8. Flowers has three games with double-digit targets, and he’s by far the No. 1 option in this passing game. Now, with Jackson expected to return, Flowers should get a major boost against a defense that has not been able to guard anyone in the passing game. (Tina MacIntyre-Yee/Rochester D&C) Mike Straw Sat, October 31, 2026 at 7:22 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Fresh off their bye, the Buffalo Bills get right back into the fight in the AFC this week with a visit from the Baltimore Ravens . There's been no shortage of classic games over the years between these two teams, who also happen to be led by two of the best quarterbacks of a generation. Buffalo heads into Sunday's game with a 5-1 record, good enough for first place in the AFC East and a tie for first in the AFC. The Ravens, however, are 4-3, sit last in the AFC North, and have their backs against the wall. That said, they are getting their best player back this week. Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games with an ankle injury, but will play against the Bills . His effectiveness remains to be seen, but he's so good that even a 75% Jackson is better than most quarterbacks in the league. Buffalo, on the other hand, has Josh Allen. The current MVP favorite is playing some of the best football of his career and has led the Bills offense to be the highest-scoring unit in football through seven weeks. But who holds the edge in the eyes of the oddsmakers? As of writing, the Bills are a -3 favorite at most sportsbooks. Some have them as much as -3.5, but it's still close either way. How big of a favorite is that? Most sportsbooks will give the home team a -3 spread when they view the game close to a pick'em. It seems to suggest, here, that if the game were in Baltimore, the Ravens could very well be the team at -2.5 or -3. If you want to look at the Moneyline, Buffalo is still favored but it's not as much as past weeks. Whereas the Bills were -245 against the Raiders, they range from -166 to -180 against Baltimore. The Ravens, on the other hand, are +145 to +150, depending on where you look. If you aren't interested in who wins, the point total is one of the highest for Week 8. Most books have the game at a 54.5 total, which is tied for the highest alongside the Dallas Cowboys and Arizona Cardinals. Both defenses have struggled this season, with the Bills only allowing less than 29 points just once this season. The Ravens have allowed at least 23 points in five of their seven games. Whatever you're interested in, Sunday's game is shaping up to be one of the best for Week 8. So, sit back and enjoy the action. The Bills and Ravens kick off at 1pm ET on CBS Sports. home.blurb: Are The Buffalo Bills Favored Against The Baltimore Ravens? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Are The Buffalo Bills Favored Against The Baltimore Ravens? (Tina MacIntyre-Yee/Rochester D&C) Mike Straw Sat, October 31, 2026 at 7:22 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Fresh off their bye, the Buffalo Bills get right back into the fight in the AFC this week with a visit from the Baltimore Ravens . There's been no shortage of classic games over the years between these two teams, who also happen to be led by two of the best quarterbacks of a generation. Buffalo heads into Sunday's game with a 5-1 record, good enough for first place in the AFC East and a tie for first in the AFC. The Ravens, however, are 4-3, sit last in the AFC North, and have their backs against the wall. That said, they are getting their best player back this week. Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games with an ankle injury, but will play against the Bills . His effectiveness remains to be seen, but he's so good that even a 75% Jackson is better than most quarterbacks in the league. Buffalo, on the other hand, has Josh Allen. The current MVP favorite is playing some of the best football of his career and has led the Bills offense to be the highest-scoring unit in football through seven weeks. But who holds the edge in the eyes of the oddsmakers? As of writing, the Bills are a -3 favorite at most sportsbooks. Some have them as much as -3.5, but it's still close either way. How big of a favorite is that? Most sportsbooks will give the home team a -3 spread when they view the game close to a pick'em. It seems to suggest, here, that if the game were in Baltimore, the Ravens could very well be the team at -2.5 or -3. If you want to look at the Moneyline, Buffalo is still favored but it's not as much as past weeks. Whereas the Bills were -245 against the Raiders, they range from -166 to -180 against Baltimore. The Ravens, on the other hand, are +145 to +150, depending on where you look. If you aren't interested in who wins, the point total is one of the highest for Week 8. Most books have the game at a 54.5 total, which is tied for the highest alongside the Dallas Cowboys and Arizona Cardinals. Both defenses have struggled this season, with the Bills only allowing less than 29 points just once this season. The Ravens have allowed at least 23 points in five of their seven games. Whatever you're interested in, Sunday's game is shaping up to be one of the best for Week 8. So, sit back and enjoy the action. The Bills and Ravens kick off at 1pm ET on CBS Sports. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. Jason Logan was already on the Over and now loves these picks for Titans vs. Bengals. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins. I was already wary of the Tennessee Titans' motivations heading into their Week 8 road date with the Cincinnati Bengals. Then Tennessee traded All-Pro DT Jeffery Simmons to Chicago Thursday afternoon. That move tacked on an extra point to this surging spread, with Cincinnati now laying -11.5 on Sunday afternoon. My Titans vs. Bengals predictions size up that mountain of chalk as well as the crater Simmons leaves in this Tennessee stop unit. Here are my best NFL picks for Nov. 1. TOP Pick Titans vs Bengals prediction: Over 46.5 One of my first plays of Week 8 was taking the Over in this game. And with Jeffery Simmons swapping out his trademark red sleeves for Chicago orange, I like the Over even more considering the Cincinnati Bengals will do the heavy lifting. Simmons was the shining star and identity of the Tennessee Titans defense. His absence up front will drop the Titans even further down the defensive pecking order, which says something when they're already dead last in DVOA at FTN . The Bengals picked apart a very good Baltimore stop unit in the second half of Sunday's win. They finished with 7.0 yards per play and were a perfect 5 for 5 in the red zone, with Joe Burrow and his talented receiving corps finding their stride. Tennessee's secondary allows the second-highest completion rate and has been burned by multiple big plays, bleeding the fourth most passes of 20+ yards entering Week 8. While the Titans haven't given up many passing touchdowns, they haven't played many QBs on Burrow's level. Titans vs Bengals combo The Bengals do the lion's share of the scoring but don't discount the Titans. Tennessee is playing with pace and faces a Cincy defense that still has work to do. Chase Brown finds the end zone to the cheers of fantasy owners everywhere. He faces a watered-down Titans defense that's allowed six scores to running backs. Tee Higgins' projections call for as many as 91 yards against a Tennessee secondary giving up explosive plays. Chase Brown touchdown Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Titans vs Bengals touchdown scorer: Chase Brown If anyone was happy to see Simmons traded before Week 8, it was Bengals running back Chase Brown. He no longer has to worry about one of the premier run stoppers in the game, facing a Tennessee red-zone defense now missing its biggest cog. Even when Simmons was in the mix, Tennessee had allowed six scores to rival RBs. Brown has only one touchdown in 2026 despite 13 carries and three receptions in the red zone. Due to that drought, we're getting a discount on his ATTD market in Week 8 considering this prop was trading around 60% two games ago. Given the massive spread, Cincinnati will be in a run-positive game script in the second half of Sunday, helping boost Brown's TD probabilities. His TD forecasts range between 60% and 78%, given he's a threat to run one in or catch a touchdown pass. Titans vs Bengals player prop: Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Cincinnati has arguably the best one-two punch at receiver in the NFL, with Tee Higgins serving as "Robin" to Ja'Marr Chase's "Batman". But don't tell Higgins that. He looked more like Superman in Week 7, putting in a monster effort in the win over the rival Ravens. He caught six of seven balls his way for 148 yards and a touchdown. That includes a 44-yard dinger on a broken play with Burrow dodging pressure. We mentioned the Titans' problems giving up home runs over the top, and Higgins is one of the best deep threats in the land, averaging 21.6 air yards per reception and amassing eight catches for 20+ yards. Tennessee has also been burned by WR2s to start the season, rating 24th in DVOA vs. WR2s at FTN while giving up almost 56 yards per game to those second options. Higgins' Week 8 models are very bullish on his receiving yards, ranging from 65 to a high of 91. Most forecasts come in above 80 yards, and my projection sits just shy of 81 yards receiving. Much of the NFL is still grading the trade, but the Cincinnati Bengals are likely relieved by the timing, as they host the Titans this week. This matchup pits two teams that seem to be going in opposite directions. Tennessee is 1-6, and their offense is struggling to gel together around quarterback Cam Ward. Meanwhile, Cincinnati just took off like a jet last week, scoring 35 unanswered against the Baltimore Ravens. It seems pretty clear-cut how this game is expected to play out, but how do oddsmakers and experts feel about it? The Bengals are currently 11.5-point favorites against the Titans, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . That is the biggest spread Cincinnati has had this season. They were only 6.5-point favorites against the Miami Dolphins coming off two straight losses. Safe to say the number got a little bigger after Tennessee traded Simmons this week. The point total is set at 46.5 points combined. The real wild card for these bets is which Bengals' defense is going to show up. Are they going to give up 200 rushing yards, or will they be able to shut it down like last week against Derrick Henry? All of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has a consensus of Cincinnati winning from their six experts None of NFL.com's five experts are taking the Titans NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick Initially, I was worried this may be a trap game at home for the Bengals. Sometimes this team will just drop a terrible game after a huge win. That happens especially when they are playing down to a bad team's level. I'm not sure how the Simmons trade might impact that, but I am hopeful the Titans are a bit more deflated coming out than fighting even harder. Either way, Burrow and this offense shouldn't have any trouble scoring and moving the ball. Their job got a lot easier without Simmons in the middle of that defense. The only thing I'm worried about offensively with the Titans is their running backs breaking off a few big runs. Bengals 41, Titans 13 Who Dey! Join Bengals fans on the SB Nation app! picks.blurb: Tennessee Titans vs. Cincinnati Bengals: Week 8 staff picks and predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams earns MVP honors College football live updates Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Tennessee Titans vs. Cincinnati Bengals: Week 8 staff picks and predictions Dan Benton, Titans Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 12:42 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Titans (1-6) will take on the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) this Sunday afternoon at Paycor Stadium in their eighth game of the 2026 regular season. Opening the week, the Titans were listed as 10-point road underdogs , but that line has gotten substantially worse with Tennessee now at +12.5. How does the Titans Wire staff see this Week 8 battle shaking out? Here's a look at our picks and score predictions. Mark Mihalko: Bengals 34, Titans 13 Uninspired after the shocking trade of Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears, the listless Titans come out and play their worst game in 2026. Cam Ward and the offense have some early moments, but the retooled defense can't slow down Joe Burrow and the explosive Bengals attack. The Bengals dominate in a 34-13 Week 8 win. Serena Burks: N/A Dan Benton: Bengals 30, Titans 10 The Titans are in fire-sale mode with eyes on the future, their best player -- defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons -- is gone, the Cam Ward experiment appears to be failing, and morale is at an all-time low. Meanwhile, the Joe Burrow-led Bengals are on a two-game winning streak and need a victory to keep pace in an unexpectedly competitive division. This one could get ugly in a hurry. Bryan Manning: Bengals 27, Titans 13 What a week for the Titans. Now, they gotta stop Joe Burrow and Cincinnati's offense without star DT Jeffery Simmons. Good luck. Plus, the Bengals' defense has been better than advertised this year after the additions of DTs Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. So, I don't feel optimistic about the Titans moving the ball against Cincinnati. Parish Sharkey: Bengals 36, Titans 20 Tony Pollard continues his momentum from his best of the season with another 100-plus yard rushing performance. However, the defensive struggles continue against the best passing threat they have faced this season as the Bengals outduel the Titans for their fifth win in their last six matchups. Kevin Hickey: Bengals 27, Titans 17 The Cincinnati Bengals should have little trouble taking care of business against the Tennessee Titans in Week 8. Cincinnati's explosive offense, led by Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins, presents a difficult matchup for a Titans defense that has struggled to consistently slow down opposing offenses. That unit is now without Jeffery Simmons as well. Although Tony Pollard is coming off a monster performance, rushing for 129 yards and three touchdowns against Cleveland, Tennessee will need more than another big game from its running back to pull off the upset. With the Titans also without rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate, expect Cincinnati to capitalize on its offensive firepower and secure a comfortable victory. Tyler Henry: Bengals 31, Titans 13 This is a mismatch for two teams going in opposite directions. The Bengals come in a half-game back of first place in a highly competitive AFC North division. I expect them to come out with a sense of urgency and take advantage of a Titans defense that just traded away their best player. I think the Titans are in for a lopsided finish in this one. home.headline: Ja'Marr Chase clears the air and Bengals are headed in the right direction in latest injury report
home.blurb: Ja'Marr Chase was back in full Thursday after missing all of Wednesday . Chase told reporters after practice he banged his ankle up during the end of the Bengals' Week 7 victory against the Baltimore Ravens. He should be all systems go for Sunday. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) did not practice at all. Dugger is already confirmed to miss this week. Giles-Harris was limited Wednesday, so he's trending toward missing Sunday's game as well. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen (rest), S Jordan Battle (hamstring), and DT B.J. Hill (rest) were each limited. The only changes for the Titans include DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) going limited after not practicing Wednesday, and running back Tony Pollard getting a rest day. Pollard ran for 129 yards and three touchdowns last week against the Cleveland Browns. Wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), the No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft, was a DNP for the second consecutive day. picks.headline: Cardinals vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: Cardinals vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams earns MVP honors College football live updates Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Cardinals vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:20 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals are staying the course with quarterback Jacboy Brissett. Meanwhile, at least one person thinks the Dallas Cowboys don't need trade deadline help. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. The Cowboys are 3-4, but they play in a woefully weak NFC East. They're still favored to win the division. It's a far different world for the Cardinals, who stand at 2-5 and are buried in last place in one of the NFL's toughest divisions, the NFC West. Let's take a look at what to expect. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cowboys QB Dak Prescott will throw 3 TD passes again Prescott didn't have to do much against the Eagles as the Cowboys ran the ball at will. But he still had three touchdown throws. This will be more of the same, with a lot of runs and Prescott finishing off drives with TD passes. No matter what Stephen A. Smith says, Prescott is still that dude. Of course, it seems like Smith will say anything to keep his show in the spotlight. He questioned whether the Cowboys still have confidence in Prescott on First Take via Sports Illustrated. "This is my interpretation," Smith said. "I believe there's a lack of confidence, supreme confidence in Dak Prescott. You believe in him, you're paying him, but in the same breath, you're understanding the importance of having that balanced running attack. Because when you just have him dropping back the pass that football, you're not satisfied with the level of production that you're getting." Whatever. The only way Prescott might not have a big game is if the Cardinals' defense gets gashed for 5-, 10-, and 20-yard TD runs. Oh, well, that is possible. The Cardinals have a rotten defense. Cowboys WR George Pickens will catch multiple TD passes Here's the trick: Prescott will be able to pick and choose who he wants to get the TD catches. And since Lamb has already been well established with six TD receptions in 2026, look for Prescott to make sure Pickens, who has two, closes the gap. With 16 fewer catches than Lamb on the season, it's not a stretch to see Pickens get double-digit grabs in this contest. Now, Pickens is banged up, but it's probably one of those mid-week no-biggies. The injuries are to his shoulder and hamstring, according to NBC Sports. "Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new," Aditya Fuldeore wrote. "He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status." Both receivers are supremely confident , as Lamb expressed, according to dallasnews.com. "I think that's pretty self-explanatory, to be honest," Lamb said. "Once we get going, I don't think there's … nah, I know for a fact, there's not a person in this league that can stop us." And Pickens said he's learning patience. "It's just super important just because that can boost the morale of the team when you just wait your turn," Pickens said. "Whether you're a running back, tight end, you make your play that boosts the offense." Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will throw for 280-plus yards It has been an up-and-down season for the veteran quarterback. But this is a game where volume will lead to yardage, even if it is in a game that winds up with a no-so-close loss. Brissett seems to be on the verge of losing his starting job. So look for him to be focused and effective at times. Head coach Mike LaFleur said the offensive issues aren't all on Brissett, according to NBC Sports. "Like I told you guys, he's still the starter," LaFleur said, via transcript from the team. "It's collective. Again, if the ball was just stagnant for 60 minutes and you couldn't even cross the 50-yard line, it'd be one thing. We've been down inside the 10-yard line 10 times over the last two games, so the ball is moving, but we have to finish jobs. Again, that starts with me, but that's a collective effort. "The players have to go execute. And I have to put them in better positions and give them the clarity to go do so. When they do have that clarity, they have to make the plays. We know that. We're not going to shy away from that. We know we have to finish the job when we're down there, and I don't even think we're having these conversations right now [if we had]." home.headline: Cowboys Activate Defensive Reinforcement Off IR Among 2 Roster Moves Before Week 8 Game
home.blurb: Locke is one of two Cowboys safeties to land on injured reserve this season, along with Jalen Thompson, who has yet to be designated to return as he deals with a hamstring issue. Schoonmaker was added on Thursday and did not practice over the last two days of the week before drawing a questionable tag. Based on the elevation of Mitchell, it's a good bet that Schoonmaker won't suit up on Sunday. The Dallas Cowboys have made a few roster moves ahead of their Week 8 game against the Arizona Cardinals. The team announced it has activated safety P.J. Locke off injured reserve, which gives Dallas' struggling defense a much-needed reinforcement for Sunday afternoon. In addition to that move, the Cowboys have elevated tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad. One of the team's offseason free-agent signings , Locke has not appeared in a game since Week 2 after suffering a foot injury in that contest that forced his placement on injured reserve. Thompson was placed on injured reserve after Week 3 and was initially expected to miss four to six weeks. He is now four weeks into that timeline, so he could be back in the next few. With Locke back, he should slot into a starting role next to Malik Hooker, which will push Alijah Clark and Markquese Bell down on the depth chart. However, don't be surprised if Clark still sees a good amount of playing time, as he has shined for Dallas in the absences of Locke and Thompson. Th elevation of Mitchell comes amid uncertainty surrounding tight end Luke Schoonmaker, who popped up on the injury report this week with a groin issue. A former fifth-round pick of the Detroit Lions, Mitchell was signed to the Cowboys' practice squad in early September after cutdown day. Assuming he plays on Sunday, this will be his first game action of 2026. Mitchell has appeared in 35 games (one start) over four seasons in the NFL and has recorded 16 catches for 169 yards. His best year was his rookie season in 2022, when Mitchell reeled in 11 receptions for 113 yards. Mitchell hasn't proven to be a reliable blocker during his four-year career, but he does have the ability to make a dent in the passing game if called upon. We'll know for sure if Schoonmaker or Mitchell will be active when the Cowboys drop their inactives at around 11:30 a.m. ET on Sunday morning. "But he's feeling as good as he can feel you know so yeah kind of go from there." Who will be blocking for him might be the bigger question. Center Hjalte Froholdt is questionable to play after being limited on Thursday with a knee injury. He did not practice on Friday. If unable to play, Hayden Conner could slide to center and the Cardinals would start a different player at right guard for the fourth time this season. Defensively, some reinforcements could be on the way. After missing the last three weeks, safety Dewey Wingard (knee) logged a full week of practice. He is questionable to play, as is cornerback Max Melton after he missed last weekend with a knee issue. Dallas ruled out wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and linebacker Dee Winters (calf). Six players are questionable to play including defensive tackle Kenny Clark (back) and wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring). Wide receiver Michael Wilson (ribs) wore the yellow non-contact pinny for a second consecutive day. He told the media on Wednesday it is out of caution. Wilson was one of eight players limited for practice. Center Hjalte Froholdt appeared on the injury report and was limited with a knee injury. His status this weekend will be important to monitor since backup center Hayden Conner is currently playing right guard. The Cowboys were back at practice on Thursday. They opened up the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard. Safety Caleb Downs (ankle), wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring), and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams (hamstring) were limited. Wide receiver Michael Wilson was wearing a yellow non-contact jersey. He appeared on the injury report with a ribs issue. He was limited. Multiple players returned to practice after being inactive on Sunday. Jeremiyah Love (ankle), safety Dewey Wingard (knee), cornerback Max Melton (knee), and quarterback Carson Beck (back) were limited. Cornerback Kei'Trel Clark was limited with an illness. Since the Cowboys did not practice on Wednesday, the designations were estimations. Wide receiver George Pickens was limited and listed with a shoulder and hamstring issue. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions will face a second straight NFC North divisional opponent when they take on the Minnesota Vikings Sunday afternoon. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . The Vikings are underdogs in this one for the second time this season. They were +4.5 underdogs in their 9-3 win in Chicago in Week 2. Detroit has now won two games in a row after falling in Carolina. The Lions blew out the Cardinals in Arizona heading into their bye and took care of business against the Packers last week. The Vikings won both meetings last season as +9.5 and +7.5 underdogs. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 8 matchup with a final score prediction. We bettors have been waiting for the right time to fade the undefeated Minnesota Vikings, and this seems like the perfect time to do it. Their offense continues to be a bottom-five unit in the league, but their defense has won them games against weak opponents.
