picks.headline: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8
picks.blurb: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams earns MVP honors College football live updates Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 4:25 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-0) own the longest active winning streak in the NFL. Dating back to November 30, 2025, they have won 11 games in a row, leaning on an exceptional defense and offense that emphasizes ball control. On Sunday, they head to Ford Field to take on the Detroit Lions (4-2), who have won two straight and are looking to stay within striking distance of the NFC North lead. The Lions' strengths are the opposite of the Vikings', ranking 2nd in scoring offense and yards per game through seven games, while no one is allowing more yards than Detroit. Minnesota's last four wins have come against teams with a combined record of 7-20. The Lions are the first opponent in a tough four-game stretch where the Vikings will play the Bills , Packers, and 49ers. Skeptics are waiting for Minnesota to come crashing back to Earth, and Sunday could be the first evidence of a regression if the Vikings' offense can't score some points. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings' matchup against the Lions. Kyler Murray will throw for over 300 yards One way you know you're making a bold prediction is if you can visualize people closing out of your article after reading. Minnesota's offense ranks 29th in passing yards. While Kyler Murray has avoided turnovers (two interceptions on 125 attempts), he hasn't consistently attacked defenses downfield. Kevin O'Connell said after last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts that the Vikings' offense is " not far off " from finding its footing. Four runs on the opening drive led to a turnover on downs, and a 3rd-and-5 on Minnesota's second drive ended in an incompletion when RG Will Fries pushed into Murray, who was ready to fire to a wide-open Justin Jefferson. Although the Vikings' defense has been elite since their 11-game winning streak began, O'Connell knows the offense will need to score to keep up with their next four opponents. Expect Murray to be less gunshy on Sunday, but here's hoping that doesn't result in recklessness. Murray goes for over 300, providing optimism moving forward that this passing attack can return to its pre-2025 self. The Vikings will intercept Jared Goff Like Murray, Lions QB Jared Goff has avoided turnovers this year. He has not thrown an interception through six games. However, Goff has still managed to complete 67.3% of his passes for 1,788 yards and 14 touchdowns for an offense that is tied for 4th-best in EPA/play. I'm not sure Minnesota can completely shut down this year's Goff, but they'll pressure him and force him into some bad plays. When the two teams last played, the Vikings forced Goff to turn the ball over five times (two interceptions, three fumbles). It may be difficult to replicate that production, but look for Brian Flores to flummox Goff into at least an extra possession. The Vikings will stop a fourth-down conversion Minnesota was somewhat susceptible to critical conversion attempts last week against Indianapolis. They allowed the Colts to convert 8-of-15 third-down attempts and their lone fourth-down attempt. Detroit converted 5-of-10 third-down attempts against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 but went 0-for-2 on fourth-down, including a controversial 4th-and-1 attempt from their own 24-yard line. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that fear of stopping the Packers' offense and gaining another possession played into last week's decision. I don't see him being nearly that aggressive from his own territory against the staunch Vikings defense. But I do think that this game will be close, forcing Campbell into a tough decision. Give me Flores' unit after they spent a week cleaning things up on the "weighty" downs. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8

away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR. away.headline: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return)
away.blurb: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return) Skip to main content SI.COM Minnesota moved to 6-0 after getting past the listless Colts, and also came out of the game relatively healthy as an added bonus. A few Vikings did leave the game with injury, though, so there are a few names to watch this week ahead of a date with the Detroit Lions. Vikings who could return in Week 8 Price took a big hit on a punt return and was evaluated for a concussion. He was cleared to return to the game, but head coach Kevin O'Connell did say that Price was dealing with a stinger after the win. It didn't seem to affect the star returner, and there shouldn't be much concern heading into Week 8. Still, Price is one of those players that is darn-near irreplaceable for the Vikings if he did have to miss time. The Vikings' first-round pick exited the game with an apparent lower-body injury. And while his name didn't come up postgame as a possible serious injury, Banks' two previous foot injuries that forced him out of football for almost a year are certainly at the forefront of fans' minds. Banks didn't return after limping off the field , and his status will be something to monitor throughout the week. Luckily, the Vikings didn't appear to lose anyone to a long-term injury on Sunday. The key Vikings out for the season remained the same with Donovan Jackson, Josh Oliver, Jamal Adams and Tyler Batty all already lost for the year. With various injuries on offense, defense and even one on special teams, here's who should be fine, and who might miss some time for Minnesota. Like Price, Addison was evaluated for a concussion before being cleared to play shortly after. Still, he wasn't able to do much in the contest, notching just two catches for 20 yards. Addison had already missed the Week 5 contest with a hamstring issue, but it appears he should have a clean bill of health to try and right the ship heading into the Lions matchup. Jones has been battling a knee injury all season, and once again aggravated it late in the game against the Colts. O'Connell called the injury day-to-day after the game, but it wouldn't be too surprising if Jones needs a week off to let things heal. The Vikings have ridden Jones hard this season with Jordan Mason's own injury issues, and the toll on his body is adding up quickly. If Jones can't shake this nagging knee issue, the Vikings could look to make a move for another runner at the trade deadline . Still, Jones has given his all this season, and it's hard to see him voluntarily coming off the field. Obviously injury concerns have been a big talking point with Banks, and if he does have to miss time, fellow rookie Domonique Orange could get some more run . Published Oct 27, 2026 TREVOR RIPLEY Trevor Ripley has covered the NFL since 2021 and is a contributing writer for Vikings On SI. But I think the Jets record reflects that he's not the answer, with their only wins coming over a hapless Titans team and a low-scoring affair against the Browns. And they're coming off handing the Dolphins their first win of the season. The same Dolphins team the Raiders put a hurting on in the opener. I see a close one here. picks.blurb: Jets vs. Raiders: 5 bold predictions for Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams earns MVP honors College football live updates Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Jets vs. Raiders: 5 bold predictions for Week 8 Geoffrey A Knox, Jets Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 12:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets are running out of opportunities to turn their season around, and Sunday's matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders presents a chance to stop the bleeding. At 2-5, Aaron Glenn's team has lost two straight games, including a frustrating divisional defeat against the previously winless Miami Dolphins . Another setback would make an already disappointing season considerably more difficult to salvage. Fortunately for New York, the Raiders aren't exactly arriving in peak condition. Las Vegas has dropped four consecutive games after opening the season 3-0, and its recent offensive struggles have created some questions of its own. Neither team can afford another afternoon of wasted opportunities, making this an interesting matchup between two teams looking to rediscover their footing. There are reasons to believe the Jets can finally put together a complete performance at MetLife Stadium. Here are five bold predictions for Week 8. Geno Smith and Garrett Wilson connect for 100-plus receiving yards and a touchdown Garrett Wilson, Jets fans, and plenty of people covering the team will be happy campers after this one. Wilson has too often been an afterthought in an offense that needs its best playmakers involved, and Sunday presents an opportunity to change that narrative. Smith and Wilson connect for more than 100 receiving yards, with the star wideout finding the end zone. After all the discussion about getting Wilson more opportunities, the Jets finally make that connection a central part of their offensive production. Ashton Jeanty finishes with fewer than 65 rushing yards Ashton Jeanty ran for 102 yards in the Raiders ' season opener, but he hasn't come close to that production since. He hasn't exceeded 58 rushing yards in any subsequent game, and his highest rushing total over Las Vegas' last three outings was just 27 yards. Now he faces a Jets defense that he decided to publicly criticize before the game. Jeanty questioned whether some New York defenders actually want to tackle, so the motivation factor shouldn't be difficult to find. The Jets respond by limiting him to 65 yards or fewer, making the Raiders running back work for everything he gets. The Jets intercept Kirk Cousins Cousins threw three interceptions combined during the first two weeks of the season before posting a clean outing in Week 3. Since then, he's developed an alternating pattern of games with an interception and games without one. He avoided a turnover against Kansas City in Week 7, which puts him in line for another costly mistake. The Jets' defense has playmakers capable of taking advantage when opposing quarterbacks become careless. Cousins has already demonstrated that he can put the football in harm's way, and New York breaks up his turnover-free streak by coming away with an interception. New York rushes for 150 yards and a touchdown The Jets enter Week 8 averaging 96.4 rushing yards per game, while Las Vegas has surrendered 143.6 yards per contest. That is a substantial difference in production, and New York has an opportunity to take advantage of a defense that has struggled to contain opposing ground attacks. The prediction calls for 150 rushing yards and at least one touchdown. Establishing the run would also help take pressure off Smith, give the offense some balance and make the Raiders defend the entire field rather than simply anticipating another passing attempt. The Jets win a back-and-forth affair New York has scored at least 23 points in three games this season. In its other four outings, the offense has failed to reach 19 points, making consistency a significant concern heading into Sunday. The Raiders need this victory just as badly, having lost four straight, so neither team should lack motivation. This one turns into a back-and-forth affair, with both offenses finding enough production to keep the outcome in doubt late. Ultimately, the Jets make a few more plays when it matters and escape with a much-needed victory. Prediction: Jets 27, Raiders 24. The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes. Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken. Both Teams Score 25 Points or More Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game. Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right? Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. picks.headline: NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns
picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams earns MVP honors College football live updates Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joey Bray Sat, October 31, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The one game standing between the 5-2 Pittsburgh Steelers and their bye week is their most consequential yet, as they are set to take on the 5-2 Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. When the ball is kicked, it will be exactly a month to the day since Cleveland took the first game between the teams on Thursday Night Football. However, the Steelers have rattled off three straight wins since then. The winner of this game will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North heading into the second half of the regular season. With both teams coming off wins and identical records, FanDuel Sportsbook gives the Pittsburgh Steelers the slight edge as a 3.5-point favorite over Cleveland. This is as close to a "must-win" game in the middle of the season for the Steelers as we will ever see. With all of that being said, here are some predictions based around my favorite prop bets of the weekend. Germie Bernard over 43.5 receiving yards TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Wide receiver Germie Bernard #17 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates the first down in the fourth quarter at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images This number is ridiculously low because the rookie receiver will be one of, if not the most targeted pass catchers on the entire team on Sunday. Last time these two teams met, Bernard got barely any playing time, but that gives him the chance to take advantage of a group that hasn't seen what he can do yet. In their first matchup, Pittsburgh had two receivers go over this total. I'm not letting last game scare me, as the Steelers controlled the clock running the football, leading to limited opportunities for any receiver. It would be a shock to see no receiver have more than three catches for the second week in a row. Bernard is a volume receiver that the Steelers will need to rely on to get open and break some tackles against their tough man defense. Rico Dowdle gets over 70 scrimmage yards TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Ifeatu Melifonwu #5 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers tackles Rico Dowdle #13 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ever since running back Rico Dowdle has returned to the lineup from his toe injury, he has looked significantly more efficient with the ball in his hands. Sure, the improved offensive line helps, but Dowdle is going to continue to earn more runs in the offense with his numbers improving. Last week, the veteran back averaged a season-high 4.6 yards per carry. Dowdle also hauled in six passes, good for the most on the team, for 45 yards. It was a more even share of the opportunities for the Steelers running backs, as Dowdle had 16 touches compared to Jaylen Warren's 21. Dowdle is the change of pace back in the Steelers offense, but is one that they will continue to use quite a bit as he gets healthier. Warren's breakout doesn't mean that Dowdle won't be involved in the offense. In fact, I think what we saw against New Orleans is what we can expect from Dowdle for the rest of the season. With the browns struggles to defend the run, both backs could be in for a big day on Sunday. Darnell Washington continues dominance with a touchdown TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Darnell Washington #80 of the Pittsburgh Steelers scores a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on a pass from Aaron Rodgers #8 during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers' six-foot-seven tight end has already set career highs in total touchdowns this season. His increased usage in the red zone is something Steelers fans have been begging to see for years now. Last week, Washington dunked on Saints defensive back Kool-Aid McKinstry as he snatched the ball out of the air from four yards out for the Steelers' only touchdown in Paris. The tight end has caught a touchdown pass in two consecutive games, and I have a hard time seeing that trend stopping against Cleveland given his continued usage in the red zone. Washington also scored against the Browns in their first matchup a month ago. It almost makes too much sense to see Washington in the end zone again on Sunday. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season. It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Falcons 24, Bucs 23 Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons. The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air. The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again. While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball. That hasn’t been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week. Overall Record: 4-3 James Hill, Writer: Falcons 21, Bucs 17 Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don’t believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it. Overall Record: 3-4 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 24, Falcons 21 The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense. Assuming Mayfield’s thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs’ offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs’ record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers. Logan Robinson, Founder: Bucs 28, Falcons 23 I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles’ rush defense, which has been excellent this year. Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta’s passing attack, it looks nice. It’s going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing. River Wells, Editor: Falcons 24, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay didn't have to pass much against the Carolina Panthers to beat them. Atlanta has a strong rushing defense, so they won't let the Bucs beat them that way — Tampa Bay will have to go through the air. I'm still not confident that Zac Robinson's offense can do that against this Falcons team. Baker Mayfeld is still recovering from injury and BIjan Robinson can change games on his own — Bucs drop this one in Raymond James. Consensus: Falcons 3, Bucs 2 This is among the closest prediction slates we've had all year. Some of us believe the Bucs will keep the momentum going, while other writers think Tampa Bay will falter as it has multiple times this year. However, the winner of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' Week 8 battle with the Atlanta Falcons will likely determine who is the favorite to win the division. At 2-5, the Bucs have been left for dead more than once this season. However, their 43-13 annihilation of the first-place Carolina Panthers has them right back in the thick of the division race. Now only one game out of first place, Tampa's season has officially risen from the dead. If the Bucs can beat the 3-4 Falcons on Sunday, they will be only half a game behind the Panthers, who fell to 3-4 with their loss to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday. However, securing a victory over Atlanta will be no easy task. The Falcons are marching into Raymond James Stadium on a high note after their 29-20 win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers last week. This crucial NFC South showdown will have a big say in who takes the division crown this season and features two teams that have walked similar paths through the season's first seven weeks. The Bucs and Falcons both had high expectations coming into the season. Both teams have talented rosters and were hoping to break free of their recent curse of mediocrity. Like the Bucs, the Falcons fell flat coming out of the gate. After two straight losses to start the season, including an embarrassing 34-3 home defeat to the Panthers in Week 2, Atlanta looked like the league's worst team. However, those losses came with starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and backup Tua Tagovailoa both injured. The Falcons were forced to start third-string Cooper Rush in the first two games before he was benched for Jack Strand. Penix returned in Week 3 and led Atlanta to a dominant 35-14 win over the Packers at Lambeau Field, followed by a 45-24 thrashing of the New Orleans Saints on the road in Week 4. In those victories, plus last week's triumph over the 49ers, the Falcons have looked like a legitimate playoff team. The Bucs have also looked like a bottom-feeder for much of the season. However, in their demolition of the Panthers and a Week 5 road upset over the Dallas Cowboys , the Bucs have also looked like a playoff team. Both teams have taken turns as Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde this season. Which version of each team will we see on Sunday? In my five keys to a Buccaneers' victory , I highlighted the need for Tampa's defense to contain superstar Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson and to find a way to stop tight end Kyle Pitts, who has been a Buc-killer his entire career. If the Bucs can do both, they have a great chance to earn their third victory of the season. If not, it could be a long afternoon for the home team. The Bucs must also give their own star RB, Bucky Irving, a healthy workload to control the clock and keep the potent Atlanta offense on the sidelines. If Irving gets 20+ touches and Baker Mayfield takes care of the ball in his second game back from a three-game absence with a broken thumb, the offense should have success. I believe the Bucs' defense, which has been strong all year, will slow the Falcons offense just enough for Tampa to get its second straight victory. I think a late Penix interception will seal the game for the Bucs. Prediction: Bucs 30, Falcons 24

away.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. home.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Friday after initially suffering his ankle injury in the second quarter of the team's Week 6 London matchup versus the Houston Texans. His absence clearly puts more pressure on a safety room that has already dealt with attrition earlier this season with Eric Murray, who dealt with a Week 4 concussion that kept him out of Week 5. Those combined injuries, between weeks 5 and 6 resulted in safety Kaevon Merriweather playing increased snaps on defense: With Johnson now out, the expectation is that Merriweather will receive his first start of the 2026 season. Meyers was listed on Wednesday and Thursday's injury report as a limited participant with only a hamstring issue, before sitting out Friday's session with an additional ankle issue that would have presumably occurred on Thursday. His status could come down to game day, with rain and a wet field in the forecast for Sunday. Running back LeQuint Allen Jr. (hamstring), defensive end Josh Hines-Allen (ankle), linebacker Jahlani Tavai (hamstring), and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) were all limited on Friday and carry no game-day injury designation. picks.headline: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams earns MVP honors College football live updates Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. picks.headline: Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup
picks.blurb: Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams earns MVP honors College football live updates Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup Cameron DaSilva, Rams Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 1:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams are taking on the Los Angeles Chargers this Sunday in their first meeting since the 2022 season. The Rams are 3-4 and looking to get back to .500, while the Chargers are still searching for their first win. To preview this game, we caught up with Chargers Wire's Gavino Borquez and asked him five questions about the team, including a final score prediction. What on earth has happened to Justin Herbert and this offense? What's gone so wrong with Mike McDaniel as the OC? Chargers Wire: The Chargers sit at 0-6 and rank dead last in the NFL in points per game (15.0) and EPA per play (-0.190). Herbert is playing the worst football of his seven seasons in the league. He has thrown 5 touchdowns and thrown 8 interceptions, tying for the league high, and has taken 21 sacks. The issues are layered. The offensive line and wide receiver group have been ravaged by injuries. Pre-snap penalties have hindered the unit. And the marriage between Herbert and McDaniel's scheme has not clicked. The two spent roughly four hours in film sessions during the bye week working on mutual accountability and finding spots to build on. We will see if it comes together on Sunday. Are there any key players the Chargers are getting back from injury this week coming off the bye? Chargers Wire: Right tackle Joe Alt is officially cleared and returning to the lineup after missing time with a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has been a full participant in practice coming out of the bye, though still navigating final clearance from a concussion, and is expected to play. Who's an underrated player on defense that the Rams should know about? Chargers Wire: While the average casual fan might not know his name, defensive tackle Teair Tart is widely respected by offensive linemen as a player they need to account for. Tart is known for his run defense prowess, but he has flashed effectively in generating interior pressure. Do the Chargers have any playmakers who can threaten the Rams defense besides Ladd McConkey? Chargers Wire: The Chargers don't possess an alpha weapon, but second-year Tre' Harris has flashed potential as a reliable deep threat . In 5 games, he has caught 15 passes on 26 targets for 225 yards, averaging an efficient 15.0 yards per reception. Though his momentum was temporarily paused by an injury suffered in Week 5 that forced him to miss the Week 6 game against the Chiefs, Harris is trending towards on Sunday. Who wins on Sunday and what's the final score? Chargers Wire: While the Chargers benefit from the return of key offensive pieces in Joe Alt and Ladd McConkey, their vulnerability lies right up the middle. The Bolts' struggling interior offensive line is poised to be the Achilles' heel in this game, allowing the Rams' defensive front to consistently collapse the pocket and get to Justin Herbert. Furthermore, even with the Chargers coming off a bye week, it's hard to tell whether they've made any meaningful offensive changes. Expect the Rams to exploit the center of the line and for their balanced offense to score three touchdowns to secure the victory. Rams 24, Chargers 16. away.headline: Two Key Chargers Players Will Return to Action in Week 8 Versus the Rams
away.blurb: Safety Derwin James Jr. remains out with a hamstring injury. This week, he reportedly had a setback, and as a result, head coach Jim Harbaugh said he’s a candidate to go on injured reserve. Left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) also won’t play. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley, both of whom have hamstring injuries, are questionable for Sunday’s contest. Garrett will be out on Sunday, as will wide receiver Davante Adams. At times, the Rams have struggled defensively — they gave up 302 passing yards last week against the Las Vegas Raiders — so perhaps there is a slight opening for the Bolts to find some success. There isn’t a whole lot the Los Angeles Chargers can do right now, or even by the end of the season, to play a lot better. The most immediate thing that would help is for them to become healthier. Starting right tackle Joe Alt hasn’t played since Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks due to a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey suffered a concussion during L.A.’s last game, which was a 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6, and he entered concussion protocol as a result. Both men returned to practice for the Chargers this week, and there is good news about their status for this Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. Alt and McConkey are on the mend In the Chargers’ final injury report for Sunday’s game, neither Alt nor McConkey are listed, which means both are expected to play, per Noah Furtado of The Athletic. While the Chargers are 0-6 and have been a disaster, the Rams haven’t exactly lived up to expectations either. The Rams have a 3-4 record despite being strong favorites to win the Super Bowl championship when the season started, and while they have had some injuries, such as the one that reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett is dealing with, they have their own problems. The Bolts currently rank last in the NFL in points per game, 28th in passing yards and last in turnovers. Quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions heading into Week 8 with eight, against just five touchdown passes. Speaking to reporters on October 26, the coach said he needed to consult the team's medical staff before making that call. Early reports suggested he might return after four weeks, but the recovery period later stretched to six weeks or longer. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported last week that Garrett was likely to return to practice, with a possible Week 8 appearance in the discussion. Opening the practice window would not guarantee an immediate return to games. The Rams would have 21 days to activate Garrett to the 53-man roster or place him on season-ending injured reserve. home.headline: Two Key Chargers Players Will Return to Action in Week 8 Versus the Rams
home.blurb: Safety Derwin James Jr. remains out with a hamstring injury. This week, he reportedly had a setback, and as a result, head coach Jim Harbaugh said he’s a candidate to go on injured reserve. Left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) also won’t play. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley, both of whom have hamstring injuries, are questionable for Sunday’s contest. Garrett will be out on Sunday, as will wide receiver Davante Adams. At times, the Rams have struggled defensively — they gave up 302 passing yards last week against the Las Vegas Raiders — so perhaps there is a slight opening for the Bolts to find some success. There isn’t a whole lot the Los Angeles Chargers can do right now, or even by the end of the season, to play a lot better. The most immediate thing that would help is for them to become healthier. Starting right tackle Joe Alt hasn’t played since Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks due to a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey suffered a concussion during L.A.’s last game, which was a 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6, and he entered concussion protocol as a result. Both men returned to practice for the Chargers this week, and there is good news about their status for this Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. Alt and McConkey are on the mend In the Chargers’ final injury report for Sunday’s game, neither Alt nor McConkey are listed, which means both are expected to play, per Noah Furtado of The Athletic. While the Chargers are 0-6 and have been a disaster, the Rams haven’t exactly lived up to expectations either. The Rams have a 3-4 record despite being strong favorites to win the Super Bowl championship when the season started, and while they have had some injuries, such as the one that reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett is dealing with, they have their own problems. The Bolts currently rank last in the NFL in points per game, 28th in passing yards and last in turnovers. Quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions heading into Week 8 with eight, against just five touchdown passes. home.headline: Chargers Injury Report Ahead of Battle of LA Against Rams
home.blurb: With that said, health in this game is going to be critical, so let's take a look at the final injury report for the Chargers with players who are out, questionable, and on track to play. Additionally, Awosika, Thompson, and Leonard did not practice all week so head coach Jim Harbaugh and the coaching staff knew that they would be without those three players as well, which like James should not have affected the game plan too much. Lastly, for Mack to be available is not a surprise at all, as he was simply resting, and as a veteran, that is fairly normal for Mack so he should be a full go against the Rams' offensive line on Sunday. So, when the game starts on Sunday, it will be interesting to see if the Chargers can come out and have a full 60-minute performance to earn their first win of the year or if the Chargers' struggles will continue and lead to a Rams win as well as the Chargers falling to 0-7. Chargers Injury Report Ahead of Battle of LA Against Rams ChargersRoundtable 94 Members • 1,527 Posts ChargersRoundtable ChargersRoundtable Related stories Denny Medley-Imagn Images Denny Medley-Imagn Images Chargers Injury Report Ahead of Battle of LA Against Rams Aiden Checketts Partner Nov 1, 2026 1:34 AM Published Nov 1, 2026 1:34 AM Taking a look at the Los Angeles Chargers injury report ahead of their matchup against the Los Angeles Rams in the battle of LA. More Videos The Los Angeles Chargers are hoping to earn their first win of the season on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams in the battle of LA , but it will not be an easy task and will no doubt take a full 60-minute performance. WR Brenen Thompson (quadricep/hamstring) Focusing on James, he was actually placed on IR on Saturday, according to Adam Schefter , which is not really a surprise when considering that it was viewed as a possibility earlier in the week . As a result of that, the Chargers will now officially be without James for at least the next four games, which adds to the fact that James has not played since Week 3. So, the Chargers will need their safety room to step up with James being placed on IR. Now, looking at the big picture for Sunday, the Chargers knew they were more likely than not going to be without James, which should not affect their game plan too much on defense. In the secondary, it is going to be interesting to see if Jackson and Shelly are going to be able to play because the Rams have a great receiver in the form of Puka Nacua, who can take advantage if the secondary is not ready to play. On the offensive side, having Harris and McConkey being on track to be in the lineup for Sunday could be huge for quarterback Justin Herbert and the offense to get on track in the passing game which is something that the offense has been unable to do all year thus far. All that said, the Chargers are in a solid position health wise heading into this matchup against the Rams, so it will ultimately come downs to which team executes better between the Chargers and the Rams.

I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. away.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
away.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. After returning to the lineup in Week 3, he suffered another setback during Wednesday’s practice ahead of the rematch with Denver. In five games this season, Delane has recorded 27 combined tackles (17 solo), three tackles for loss, five pass breakups, and one interception. He’s also played nearly every defensive snap since returning in Week 3. Delane has become the Chiefs’ primary shutdown corner, while Sneed provides experience and flexibility to move around the defensive backfield. away.blurb: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker is returning to the NFL at the age of 36. Tucker is considered to be one of the greatest kickers in NFL history, which makes sense considering he's made 89.1% of his field goal attempts. His time with the Ravens ultimately came to an end after he was accused of inappropriate behavior during massage sessions. The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists made accusations against Tucker, with two of the massage parlors claiming they banned him because of his behavior. "I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider," Tucker told OutKick . "I absolutely respect the massage therapy profession and more so the individuals who work as massage therapists." Tucker has conducted workouts with the Colts, Jets and Saints over the past two years. It wasn't until this Wednesday, however, that he landed a deal. According to Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star, the Chiefs are signing Tucker to their practice squad. BALTIMORE, MARYLAND – DECEMBER 12: Kicker Justin Tucker #9 of the Baltimore Ravens talks to his wife, Amanda Bass, before playing against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on December 12, 2019 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images)Patrick Smith/Getty Images Harrison Butker has made plenty of big-time kicks for the Chiefs over the past decade, but he seems to be on the decline. Butker has made 11 of 16 field goal attempts this season. He had two crucial misses on Sunday night against the Seahawks. If Tucker outperforms Butker at practice, he could end up starting as early as this Sunday against the Broncos.

home.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
home.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. More news : Jonathan Taylor Trade Talks Heat Up as Colts Change Their Stance Delane, the Chiefs’ sixth overall pick, initially injured his right shoulder during the offseason and aggravated it in the season opener against Denver. After returning to the lineup in Week 3, he suffered another setback during Wednesday’s practice ahead of the rematch with Denver. In five games this season, Delane has recorded 27 combined tackles (17 solo), three tackles for loss, five pass breakups, and one interception. He’s also played nearly every defensive snap since returning in Week 3. More news : NFL to Review New Allegations Against Packers Star Josh Jacobs More news : Jets Send Clear Message on Garrett Wilson Amid Trade Buzz Losing both players is a tough blow to Kansas City’s secondary, particularly against a division rival that’s found its rhythm over the past few weeks. home.headline: Broncos' Week 8 Injury Report Discouraging Sign for Jaylen Waddle
home.source: Denver Broncos On SI on MSN
home.blurb: Denver listed wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), and defensive end Zach Allen (hip) — all starters — as "DNP" (Did Not Practice) following Wednesday's session. Hufanga remains on the wrong side of questionable after missing the last two games due to an ankle injury. The former AFC Defensive Player of the Week will need to get in at least limited practices on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at suiting up versus Kansas City. Allen's apparently hamstring ailment is a new development, though one that, as of this writing, seems unlikely to hold him out of Week 8 action. Elsewhere on the injury report, left tackle Garett Bolles (hip) and wide receiver Marvin Mims (ankle) were considered limited, while cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) were full participants. Surtain appears poised to return from a three-game absence as his ankle presumably is at or near full health. Of note on the Chiefs' end, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (personal/knee) did not practice on Wednesday while receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) and tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) were full goes. “I think to his credit, whenever we ask something of him—whether it’s intermediate, down the field—he’s been really effective," he said of Mims on Wednesday. "Obviously as a returner, that first return with the ball midfield, those are... I’ve said this before, the receiving now to start the game. [At] minimum there’s a threshold, but to start where we started, those are things that he’s shown us consistently. He continues to have those touches and then where you want to even get him more touches. It’s sometimes a challenge, but certainly he’s deserving.” The Denver Broncos released their initial Week 8 injury report ahead of Sunday's pivotal home showdown against the Kansas City Chiefs. An earlier report indicated that Waddle suffered a re-aggravation of a prior chest issue toward the end of last week's victory over the Arizona Cardinals, and his status for Sunday's game is to be determined. The injury occurred on a trick play that head coach and offensive playcaller Sean Payton consequently apologized for. "Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call? ... It was awful. I'm sorry," Payton said in his postgame press conference on Sunday. "If you look it up, in 2008, in a similar situation — even a more radical reverse — fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play." Rice recorded 79 receptions for 938 yards and seven touchdowns in 16 games during his rookie season in 2023. His reception and touchdown totals set Chiefs rookie records. He also had more than 100 receiving yards in two games. In the playoffs, Rice caught eight passes for 130 yards and two touchdowns against the Miami Dolphins in the Wild Card round. He finished the postseason with 26 receptions for 262 yards, setting franchise rookie records in both categories. Rice appeared in four games in 2024, recording 24 receptions for 288 yards and two touchdowns. In 2025, he played eight games and finished with 53 receptions for 571 yards and five touchdowns, along with 20 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown. It's likely to be a tough day for Willis if they get ahead too, as their secondary is so much stronger than our receiver room. We need to keep it close and run the ball well to have a chance. I'll say pats by 10 finfanfromsiam points to this team's long-standing issue covering any decent TEs. Does NE have TEs?? Nuff said…… CluelessNFLfan says that reality sets back in with another loss. The Phins come back down to earth this week. Pats 24, Phins 17. Robert Burstein has Miami losing by two TD's. I do think Miami can keep this game a little close until half time, but overall I think D.Maye will have a big game passing and making plays running. I've got Miami losing 13-27. Jptapt is being positive. Molly Polly II sees another upset on the horizon. I'm calling for an upset…why not! Patriots are favored +7.5. Defense tightens up shot group, Ollie beast mode another 100+ yards. Malik playing at home, confident, ready to prove he's the guy who can lead this team. Huge upset, Finz win with seconds left on the clock, 26-24! 🐬🐬 Gusman says it might be close, or Maye might just make the Dolphins' secondary look silly. If Drake Maye plays as he has for the past 4 games he should carve up the Dolphins secondary. Miami should be able to limit the Pats run game. Pats will attempt to shutdown Miamis run game forcing the Dolphins into passing situations. The Pats have a much better secondary than the Phins. Best bet for Miami is to hope Maye is sloppy and throws a couple picks and loses a fumble or two. The Pats are coming off a 10 day break and are not taking a Miami victory for granted. Should be a fairly close entertaining game. picks.blurb: Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams earns MVP honors College football live updates Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:29 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami. Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly. He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville. Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers. It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season. Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways. The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs. Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game. Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone. Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13 The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not. Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge. The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games. It's been a largely disappointing first half of the season for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his debut campaign with the New England Patriots . Things are possibly about to get worse for the Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. New England could potentially afford to sit Brown in Week 8 if he's not healthy enough, as the Patriots are heavy road favorites for Sunday's contest versus the Miami Dolphins. New England has a pair of NFC North contenders on deck in Weeks 9 and 10 with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, respectively, before its Week 11 bye. The Patriots are just 4-3 this fall, however, so if they want to make a run at their second straight AFC East crown and put pressure on the Buffalo Bills (5-1), they can't take the Dolphins for granted. Brown has played in just three of New England's first seven contests this year as he missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 due to a high-ankle sprain. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to action in Week 6 against the New York Jets but has yet to have an impact on offense. Brown has played only 132 offensive snaps in his three games and has recorded nine catches for 101 scoreless yards on 20 targets. His longest reception of the season has gone for just 18 yards, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that he isn't concerned about the 29-year-old's lack of production. Thursday's news still leaves the door open for Brown to take the field and perhaps turn things around on Sunday, but it's not looking great.

away.headline: Patriots injury analysis: Pats get a much-needed reprieve in Week 7
away.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. The offseason trade acquisition has caught just six passes since his return from injury. Unfortunately, the play did not end up mattering — kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long field goal to effectively ice the game — while the sixth-year defensive tackle remained on the ground afterwards: he had landed awkwardly on his right hand and required medical assistance. Barmore walked off the field and with the Patriots playing no more defensive snaps did not get an opportunity to reenter the game. What this means for the Patriots While the injuries to both Kevin Byard and Christian Barmore could have been potentially concerning, it appears neither will be a long-term issue. Byard returned to the game, while head coach Mike Vrabel said about Barmore on Monday that “he’ll be fine.” Him and Barmore both being present at practice on Monday is concrete proof of that. home.headline: Patriots Get Good News on Injured $42 Million Lineman Before Dolphins Game
home.blurb: Vera-Tucker exited in the second quarter of New England's Week 6 victory over his former team, the New York Jets , on Oct. 18 and did not return. New England ruled him out for Thursday night's game against the Chicago Bears, according to ESPN , then moved him to injured reserve Oct. 22 . That designation sidelines him for Weeks 7 through 10 at minimum, with a return at least possible in Week 12 after the bye. Before the move, he had started five games and 340 offensive snaps , according to The Boston Globe . Injuries, unfortunately, have shaped his career. A torn right triceps ended his 2022 season in Week 7, according to Sportsforecaster.com , and a torn Achilles did the same in Week 5 of 2023. He started 15 games in 2024 , then tore his left triceps in practice before Week 1 of 2025, wiping out his entire season . The injury epidemic cost the unit continuity and depth. Vrabel's comments leave room for Vera-Tucker to rejoin it later this season, with Week 12 the earliest possible return. Whether his hamstring cooperates by then is the question Vrabel could not answer Monday.
