The Philadelphia Eagles hit the road to play the Washington Commanders, and both of these teams are struggling right now in the NFC East. However, if you don’t want to pick a winner for this game or even the total, you can simply take a player to find the end zone and potentially come away as a winner on Sunday night. There are a bunch of different players to consider in this market, but the Eagles' offense has been banged up all year with DeVonta Smith (out) and Saquon Barkley (set to play despite a hamstring injury) missing time. That has thrust some lesser-known players into big roles, especially with Jalen Hurts out for the season with a blood clot. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee is set to make his third consecutive start, and the Eagles are looking to snap a five-game losing streak that has dropped them into third place in the division. Meanwhile, the Commanders are coming out of their bye week and looking to get back on track after a loss on Monday Night Football in Week 6 to the San Francisco 49ers. Jayden Daniels and company lost Terry McLaurin to a knee injury for the rest of the season in that matchup, which should lead to some new faces carrying the load for Washington at receiver. That opens the door for some interesting decisions in the anytime touchdown scorer market, and I've decided on three players that I like to score with these two rivals facing off. Here's a breakdown of each of those picks and their latest odds for Week 8's Sunday night showdown. Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Eagles vs. Commanders Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Saquon Barkley Anytime TD (+130) Washington is 31st in the NFL in EPA/Rush this season, so this is an ideal matchup for Saquon Barkley (back, hamstring) if he’s able to play. The star running back scored a touchdown in Week 7 against the Dallas Cowboys, but he played limited snaps in that matchup. Overall, Barkley has suited up for just 32.8 percent of the Eagles’ offensive plays in the five games he’s appeared in, making him a risky bet elsewhere in the prop market. The star back played less than 16 percent of the snaps in Week 7, but he still handled nine touches for 71 yards and a score. The Commanders have only given up five rushing scores in six games, but they may struggle to contain Barkley, even if he’s at less than 100 percent. Stefon Diggs Anytime TD (+215) Stefon Diggs has four touchdown catches in five appearances in the 2026 season for the Commanders, and he’s now the No. 1 receiver with McLaurin done for the year. Diggs has played just 59.8 percent of the Commanders’ snaps on offense, yet he’s been targeted at least six times in every game. That’s led to 24 receptions for 214 yards, and Jayden Daniels has thrown the ball Diggs’ way a ton this season. In fact, Diggs found the end zone and had nine targets against this Philly team in Week 1. I’m buying him to have another big game on Sunday night, especially after he stepped up for six grabs and a score in Week 6. Dallas Goedert Anytime TD (+220) Earlier this season, Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert had four catches for 77 yards and two scores in a Week 1 win over Washington. He has not found the end zone since, but the veteran tight end has remained a big part of the offense. Over the last two weeks with McKee at quarterback, Goedert has been targeted 15 times, catching 11 passes for 109 yards. That workload should eventually turn into some scores, and this is a great matchup for the Eagles tight end to make it happen. Through six games, the Commanders have allowed eight receiving scores to the tight end position. Only the Detroit Lions (10) have allowed more. Goedert is a great bet to lead an otherwise banged up Philadelphia offense in Week 8. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee. The battle of the NFC East basement sees the Philadelphia Eagles visiting the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football. This division has been a mess in the first two months of the schedule, but Week 8 goes a long way to defining the second half of the schedule. My Eagles vs. Commanders predictions see SNF swinging in a different direction than the current markets would suggest, which is kind of on par with this upside-down division. Here are my favorite NFL picks for prime time on Nov. 1. TOP Pick Eagles vs Commanders prediction: Over 40.5 If you read my weekly NFL Underdogs column , you'll see I'm taking the points with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. A big reason why is this underrated offense. Yes, Philadelphia has a backup under center and is potentially missing its top two WRs again. Yet, the Eagles have looked capable with Tanner McKee at the wheel. And with Saquon Barkley back, they went blow-for-blow with Dallas for 45 minutes on Monday until running out of ammo in the final frame. The Washington Commanders defense doesn't put up much of a fuss. Washington is a bottom-tier team in several key defensive measurements , including third-down conversions and red-zone defense. Making up for the soft stop unit is an offense that should at least be able to keep its quarterback clean. Philadelphia's once-vaunted pass rush is no more, boasting the fifth-lowest pressure rate , and that means Jayden Daniels has time in the pocket. Daniels is now four weeks returned from his elbow injury, with a bye in Week 7, and is coming off his best performance of the season. He passed for 300 yards and 72.5% completions with two TDs in a loss to San Francisco on Oct. 19. Eagles vs Commanders combo There's a lot of big-name firepower missing on both sides, but I see more meat on the bone for these offenses – especially considering that the complementing stop units are both garbage. Washington allowed Dallas Goedert to find the end zone twice in Week 1 and have given up the second most TDs to tight ends heading into Week 8. With the Eagles' receiving corps running thin, Goedert's role spikes on SNF. Rookie WR Antonio Williams is filling the void left by Terry McLaurin, doing plenty of damage out of the slot. He burned Philly in his NFL debut and is projected for as many as 46 receiving yards in Week 8. Dallas Goedert touchdown Antonio Williams 30+ receiving yards Eagles vs Commanders touchdown scorer: Dallas Goedert With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks still hurting, tight end Dallas Goedert sees a spike in his involvement in the passing game. Goedert drew seven targets for five receptions in Week 7 and has been McKee's safety blanket during his two-game stint as the starter. The Eagles face a Commanders defense that has been bullied by rival tight ends this season. Washington ranks dead last in DVOA vs. tight ends, allowing the seventh most yards to the position along with eight touchdowns to TEs in just six games. Goedert is responsible for two of those touchdowns, with a pair of scores in the win over Washington in Week 1. His touchdown forecasts for this return matchup range from 19% to as high as 44%, with the majority at 30% or higher. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions in the Commanders' Showdown With the Eagles, Starting With Jayden Daniels - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams earns MVP honors College football live updates Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Nishant Gupta Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders get their rematch with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night, and very little about it looks like the opener. Philadelphia won that one 24-22 when Washington's tying two-point try was stuffed. Since then, Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, and the Eagles have lost five straight, their longest skid since 2016. Washington (1-4-1) comes off its bye after a 23-17 loss in San Francisco that also cost it Terry McLaurin, who tore his patellar tendon and is done for the season, according to the team . Head coach Dan Quinn called the week off "a much-needed reset in a lot of ways," per the team's website . Philadelphia (2-5) lost 38-21 to Dallas on Monday night with Tanner McKee at quarterback. The Commanders are about a six-point favorite at Northwest Stadium and hold the EPA edge in nine of 12 categories. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday Night Football. Jayden Daniels leads Washington in rushing Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) is hit as he throws by San Francisco 49ers defensive end Romello Height (94) during the second quarter at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Daniels has 213 rushing yards on 25 carries, 8.5 per attempt, in four games, and his 88.7 rushing grade ranks third among quarterbacks, according to PFF . He has played the last two games in a brace after dislocating his left elbow in Week 2, and he ran only four times for 10 yards in San Francisco. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Washington needs him to run. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve with a groin injury , leaving Rachaad White (36 carries, 145 yards) as the lead back. Philadelphia ranks 27th against the run at 131.4 yards per game, and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards against the Eagles on Monday. Bold prediction: Daniels runs for 75 yards and a touchdown, more than any Washington running back. Washington sacks Tanner McKee four times Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Washington Commanders linebacker Odafe Oweh (98) sacks Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) during the first quarter at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Quinn's defense blitzes more than any team except Minnesota, and it has only 11 sacks, tied for 22nd. "I'd love to see us, whether it's blitzing or rush coverage together, really being in sync with that," Quinn said Wednesday, per the team's website . Odafe Oweh leads the team with three sacks on 15 pressures, according to PFF , though he hasn't played up to his contract yet. K'Lavon Chaisson has 2.5 sacks and two forced fumbles. McKee is working behind a line that has allowed 18 sacks, and the Eagles had no sacks or quarterback hits of their own against Dallas. Bold prediction: Washington sacks McKee four times, even with Javon Kinlaw likely out with a knee injury. Antonio Williams beats Zack Baun this time Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams (14) makes a catch during the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Week 1 belonged to Zack Baun. Washington targeted him six times in coverage, and its pass catchers finished with minus-2 yards against him, per Next Gen Stats. He added 12 tackles and was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week . Baun is still fifth among linebackers with a 79.5 grade, but he has allowed a 100.0 passer rating in coverage, according to PFF . With McLaurin out, the rookie is the receiver Washington needs to change the equation . Antonio Williams has 18 catches for 205 yards and a touchdown, and he caught four passes for 64 yards and a score in the opener. Bold prediction: Williams goes over 75 yards, and at least one of those catches comes with Baun in coverage. Sonny Styles forces a turnover Sept. 27, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders linebacker Sonny Styles (52) gets the tackle and forces a fumble by Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price (8) in the first quarter at Northwest Stadium. Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Sonny Styles leads Washington with 46 tackles and has an interception, a sack and a forced fumble. He made 13 tackles in San Francisco, per NBC Washington , and his 72.7 coverage grade ranks 10th among linebackers, according to PFF . Philadelphia's offense ranks 29th in EPA, and Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks all missed practice Thursday, per the Eagles . That could leave McKee leaning on Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon over the middle, where Styles does his work. Washington is plus-6 in turnover differential, second in the NFL . Bold prediction: Styles forces a fumble or picks off McKee. They were embarrassed Monday against Dallas. They got a solid performance from their injury-ravaged offense, but their defense was bullied, plain and simple. The players on that defense know they were pushed around, and they know they weren't anywhere near good enough. It's not going to be the prettiest game – these two games have three wins in 13 combined games – but I think the Birds make just enough plays on defense to nose out the Commanders. away.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Eagles release lengthy injury report to start Week 8 – NBC Sports Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles released another lengthy injury report to begin Week 8 prep for the Commanders. By Dave Zangaro • Published October 28, 2026 • Updated on October 28, 2026 at 7:33 pm The Eagles, losers of five straight games, released another CVS receipt-length injury report as they began their prep to face the Commanders on the road on Sunday Night Football. Because the Eagles held a walkthrough to begin their short week after playing on Monday night, this injury report is an estimation. But both Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) were among the players listed as non-participants: Full: LB Zack Baun (shoulder), CB Jakorian Bennett (knee), G Landon Dickerson (pectoral), OLB Arnold Ebiketie (shoulder), TE Dallas Goedert (knee), C Drew Kendall (knee), G Tyler Steen (shoulder) Earlier on Wednesday, the Eagles placed RB Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. We’ll obviously monitor that this week because when Barkley was on the field against the Cowboys, he was very good. Both Smith (hamstring) and Wicks (ankle) missed the Cowboys game and could be in danger of missing this upcoming game against the Commanders. The Eagles have just two games before their bye week. Campbell (hamstring/quad), Covey (knee) and Jones (hamstring) are additions to the injury report this week. If Campbell is unable to play on Sunday, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. would start next to Zack Baun. Without Covey, Makai Lemon took over as the Eagles’ punt returner on Monday. away.headline: Seattle Seahawks RB Jadarian Price Looking Ready for the Chicago Bears
away.blurb: Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price practiced fully on Friday as he attempts to return from the chest injury that placed him on injury reserve. The Seattle Seahawks could see the return of Price and Zach Charbonnet on Monday when they play the Chicago Bears. Charbonnet was limited in practice on Friday, but he practiced fully on Thursday. With both running backs in good standing thus far this week, the Seattle Seahawks can finally showcase their new-look rushing attack without Kenneth Walker III. The Seattle Seahawks drafted Price with the final pick of the first round in the 2026 NFL Draft. While the early returns from Price are limited, the small sample size showed how impactful his presence was to Seahawks starting quarterback Sam Darnold. On early downs, Darnold owns 10-13 completion ratio with 138 yards passing and a touchdown with Price on the field. Not to mention, Price’s rushing efficiency should only increase with Charbonnet also in the fold. The threat of two running backs will keep defenses guessing as to what the Seattle Seahawks are going to do since both are threats in the passing game as well. It seems likely that the Seahawks have their projected running back room healthy in week eight against the Chicago Bears. The Bears rank 19th in rushing EPA allowed, so a heavy running game will be necessary. Seattle Seahawks Running Back Jadarian Price Practices Fully Before Monday’s Bears Game Another issue that plagues Price so far in his rookie season are fumbles. In three games, he dropped the ball onto the ground twice, which was an issue previously for him as well in college at Notre Dame. The Seattle Seahawks have struggled with turnovers in general though, so this is not necessarily an issue that is exclusive to Price. That being said, with the addition of Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts , Price should be entering a situation where he can succeed right away. The Seattle Seahawks want to establish a physical identity at the line of scrimmage. They have that defensively, no doubt. However, offensively, that identity still formulates. The excellence of Jaxson Smith-Njigba cannot be understated, and the Seahawks will continue with him as their focal point as they should. However, the importance of the running game cannot be understated to limit the pass attempts for Darnold. The Seahawks Running Game Finally Comes Into Focus This Season In week seven’s victory over the Kansas City Chiefs , running back Emanuel Wilson ran for 100 yards on 24 carries. The Seahawks ability to run the ball against an above average Chiefs defense should not be ignored, especially when lacking their top two backs. Regardless of the availability of Charbonnet and Price, the Seahawks running game has risen from the grave . Now, they face the team that defeated the Patriots in last season's Super Bowl, the Seattle Seahawks, on Monday night. The trip to Seattle will be the Bears' second Monday Night Football assignment of the season already, but they may be getting a boost to their running game before they face the Seahawks — who derailed the NFL's leading rusher, Kenneth Walker III, in Sunday's win over the Kansas City Chiefs. According to an early report, running back Kyle Monangai could be on his way back to playing status after missing three straight games with a turf toe diagnosis. Monangai has a better chance of playing against Seattle Monday night, according to ESPN 's Jeremy Fowler, than he has since coming down with the injury on Oct. 8. Whether Fowler's read proves accurate depends on Thursday's first injury report, because Monangai skipped the open portion of Tuesday's practice and Chicago promoted another running back to the active roster. "During the open portion of practice, we did not see RB Kyle Monangai," Chicago Tribune reporter Sean Hammond wrote, on Tuesday . The Bears also promoted Zavier Scott from the practice squad after he used his three game-day elevations, according to the Chicago Sun-Times . Fowler is ESPN's senior NFL reporter and SportsCenter insider , and he has handled Monangai news before. In August, he reported that Monangai was expected to miss multiple weeks with a hyperextended knee and Johnson called Monangai week to week .
